{
  "thinking": "Maya has the pad and a fish plan that works: start at the nose, run the top and bottom edges back, and branch the tail off the back. I missed my chance to pitch a fish, so I'll back hers and suggest a forked tail so the judge can read it as a fish.",
  "say": "Fish works for me, Maya. Starting at the nose is good, since the run flows one way from there. Could we make the tail a clear fork rather than a single fin? That split is what says fish when it falls. I can take the tail once the body's down.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 5,
  "point": [6, 10],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Team is building a fish from Maya's pad sketch: start at the nose (left end), top and bottom edges run back to the right, tail fin branches off the back. I suggested a forked tail. Offered to take the tail once the body is down. Watch the start: it must be the nose end, and all lines should leave in the same direction."
